Subject: Quick ask — observability add-on economics

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the dashboards looked promising. Before we take this to procurement I need a clear breakdown of cost for the observability add-ons you mentioned: retention tiers, tracing sampling/ingest fees, and the advanced dashboards (both seat-based and tenant-level).

High-level numbers we care about: 12 month committed baseline, expected peak QPS ~120r/s, daily token generation ~2.7M, and about 6 heavy user seats for dashboards. Could you put together a simple pricing table (slab vs metered examples), and call out any pilot credits or one-time migration fees? Procurement will also want a sample SOW for a 3-month pilot.

If you can send the tiered examples and a recommended concession schedule for an enterprise trial (we may ask for something like a 30% credit for first 3 months), that would help us move quickly.

Appreciate it — Michael

--
Michael Lewis
VP, Engineering Operations
Atria Health
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Quick ask — observability add-on economics

Michael / Sara,

Thanks — attaching a concise package. Highlights in short:

- Retention: two primary constructs we recommend for Atria:
  1) Slab (monthly included GBs) — predictable for steady-state log/trace volume; recommended when long-term storage & replay are needed. Example: 5TB/month slab priced at $X/GB with 10% discount at 12-month commit.
  2) Metered (pay-as-you-go) — works for bursty workloads and short retention windows. Example: $Y/GB ingest + $Z/GB/month for storage.

- Tracing: ingest-based pricing with a sampling credit model. We propose a sampling floor that buys a guaranteed tail-latency trace capture rate; additional sampled spans bill per million spans.

- Advanced dashboards: two options — seat-based ($/seat/month) for power users; or tenant-level flat fee for org-wide dashboards. For Atria (6 heavy seats), seat model is likely cheaper initially; tenant fee recommended if you plan to expand to >25 heavy seats or enable dashboard sharing across multiple business units.

- Pilot: we can do a 3-month pilot with a 75% usage credit on retention (up to 2TB/month), waived SOW setup fee, and a single custom dashboard build included. After pilot, credits step down per the concession schedule in the attachment.

I attached: Redwood_Observability_Pricing_v1.xlsx (tier examples + sample invoice) and a draft SOW for a 3-month pilot (SOW_Pilot_Atria.pdf).

If it helps, I can set a short call with our pricing lead (Ben) and product (Kim) to walk procurement through the sample invoice later this week.

Best,
Sofia

--

Quick proposal for the concession schedule:

- Pilot (3 months): 75% retention credit up to 2TB/month (as Sofia suggested). Waive one-time SOW setup fee ($12k).
- Transition month (month 4): 50% credit on overage up to an additional 1TB to reduce spike risk.
- Year 1 renewal: if they convert to a 12-month commit at >= 5TB/month, offer a 10% committed discount on both slab and seat fees.
- Guardrails: credits apply only to retention/storage charges and not to tracing per-span fees or seat licensing. Credits are non-transferable and expire if not converted within the first 6 months after pilot.

Invoice presentation idea (sample lines):
- Observability slab: Included 5TB @ $0.035/GB = $1790/mo (example)
- Retention overage: billed per GB beyond included slab
- Tracing: $X per million sampled spans (with sampling floor of 250k spans/day)
- Dashboards: $75/seat/month or $2,500/tenant/month (choose lower-cost seat model for 6 seats)
- One-time migration/setup: $12,000 (waived for pilot)

Recommend we keep the pilot caps explicit and include a simple conversion table so procurement can model after credits expire. Happy to walkthrough the invoice on a call.

- Ben
